format_content.content: The course is a four-part Java series, each part about three to four hours long.
The first part teaches the fundamentals of programming with Java.

events.event: A while loop checks its condition before executing the loop body, so if the condition is false the body never runs. A do-while loop checks the condition after executing the body, guaranteeing that the body runs at least once even when the condition is false.

events.event: When Java sees the break statement it will ignore everything else after and it will terminate the loop.

format_content.content: When Java sees the continue statement it moves control to the beginning of the loop, causing the remaining statements in the current iteration to be ignored.
The break statement terminates a loop.
The continue statement moves control to the beginning of a loop.
Using `true` as the loop condition creates an infinite loop that runs until a break statement terminates it.

steps: Read user input inside the loop.
If the input equals "quit", execute a break statement to terminate the loop.
If the input equals "pass", execute a continue statement to skip printing and start the next iteration.

format_content.definition: A loop construct in Java used to iterate over arrays or collections without needing an explicit index or counter.
A loop that never terminates on its own, typically created with a condition that is always true (e.g., while true) unless a break statement is used.

format_content.content: The for each loop can only iterate forward through an array and does not provide access to the index of each element.
When using while true, a break statement must be included inside the loop body to prevent an infinite loop that never terminates and can consume memory.

format_content.content: A for each loop in Java iterates over arrays or collections without requiring an explicit counter.
The for each loop iterates only in the forward direction; it cannot iterate from the end to the beginning of an array.
A while true loop without a break statement results in an infinite loop that never terminates.

format_content.definition: Statements like if and switch for making decisions in programs, and loops for executing code repeatedly.

format_content.content: Control flow is managed using comparison operators, logical operators, and three types of control flow statements: conditionals (if, switch) and loops (for, while, do‑while, foreach), as well as break and continue for altering loop execution.
Long methods reduce maintainability; breaking code into smaller, readable chunks improves understandability and makes it easier for others to work with the code.
Breaking code into smaller chunks makes it easier to read and understand.
Clean code is valued because it is understandable by humans, not just computers.
